headings.title: SMTO-LLM-0017 — The model used up its reply space without giving an answer

html:
SMTO-LLM-0017 — The model used up its reply space without giving an answer

GUID: 8b947f76-80cc-49f4-a048-218ac967334a
Slug: model-output-truncated-no-action
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: provider

What happened

  • The model hit its output limit before writing any answer or action. This can happen when its hidden thinking uses up the space. SMTO had nothing it could use, so nothing was carried out.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Below the message box, turn Thinking off or lower its budget for this conversation (select Controls if you don't see it). Thinking counts toward the same output limit, so less thinking leaves room for the answer.
  2. Or raise the Output limit slider next to it. More room lets the model finish thinking and still write its answer.
  3. Ask SMTO to continue in a new message, saying which steps are already done. These changes apply to new messages, and the empty reply did nothing that needs undoing.

What success looks like

  • The model replies with an answer or starts an action instead of this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the model; it may need different thinking settings on the model server. Don't change unrelated settings such as timeouts; they don't affect this limit.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The provider stopped with finish_reason "length" but returned no answer text, tool name or tool arguments, so there was no usable decision (model_output_truncated_no_action).

What this means

  • The provider reported an output-length stop with no answer text, tool name or tool arguments. The allowance may have been consumed by output that is not actionable, but this category does not establish why. There is no complete instruction from this response to execute.

Why this can happen

  • The finish reason is length and the counted visible answer and tool-call fields are empty.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the output allowance and reasoning settings with a small provider test. Check supported tool output before assuming a larger allowance will solve the problem.

How to fix it

  • Compare the effective output limit, thinking settings and reasoning counts in provider_diagnostic with a small provider test. Change only the setting that prevented usable output: reduce thinking (composer Thinking or the role's thinking parameters) or raise the role's Output allowance; captured task settings apply to new tasks, so start a new task after changing them.
  • Compare the captured output allowance and reasoning settings with a small provider test. Change only the setting shown to prevent usable output, then start a new task if a captured setting changed. Keep earlier completed results.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The next test returns nonempty usable output and a supported completion reason.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • The current decision is rejected before tool authorization when enforcement applies; earlier results are not replayed.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
